criterion: error and rollback paths / partial-failure handling
finding: A Refused raised after writes reports 'nothing was written' with exit 1, though a ticket and a comment exist
why: For a ticket this run creates, the in-review target is only resolved inside _execute (line 743), and its Refused is caught at line 336-338 as 'REFUSED: ...; nothing was written' / exit 1, which BUG-MODE.md defines as 'refused, nothing written'.
fix: Raise Failed (exit 2) for any check that fails after the first write, or resolve what can be resolved before the first write and state that the created-ticket in-review match is checked after create.
evidence: Probe (stub Jira whose new ticket offers only 'Start (11)', config jira.transitions.in-review=31, in_review=True): code=1; lines 'STEP: ticket — PROJ-1 created', 'STEP: evidence — comment posted', 'REFUSED: PROJ-1 offers no transition matching the in-review value `31`; it offers: Start (11); nothing was written'; writes ['tracker_create','tracker_comment']. Code: `if plan.target is None: ... plan.target = _in_review_target(run, plan.key, value)` and `except Refused as e: lines.append(f"REFUSED: {e}; nothing was written"); return Result(1, lines)`.

criterion: changed pre-existing sentence true of the code it describes (CHANGELOG.md)
finding: CHANGELOG says the in-review state is checked before any write, but on a created ticket the transition match runs after create and its refusal reports 'nothing was written'
why: publish_bug_mode.py:417 only resolves the in-review target when a key exists before the run; for a create, _move_to_in_review (lines 741-743) calls _in_review_target after the ticket, evidence and proof writes, and its Refused is caught at lines 336-338 as 'REFUSED: ...; nothing was written' with exit 1, so the operator is told nothing was written when a ticket exists (the same mislabel hits _write_part's Refused at line 214 during _execute); no test covers create + --in-review with no matching transition (tests only cover the existing-key case at test_publish_bug_mode.py:428-434).
fix: Raise Failed (exit 2, 'no write followed it') for any check that fails inside _execute, and either drop 'in-review state ... before any write' from the CHANGELOG/BUG-MODE refusal list for the create path or add a test pinning the create + --in-review refusal.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:54-55 "It checks the type, the key, the in-review state and the fix version before any write"; publish_bug_mode.py:417-418 "if in_review and target_key:\n        target = _in_review_target(run, target_key, str(value))"; :741-743 "if plan.target is None: ... plan.target = _in_review_target(run, plan.key, value)"; :336-337 "except Refused as e:\n        lines.append(f\"REFUSED: {e}; nothing was written\")"

criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: Spinoff step 3 still calls the tracker_create description plain text and names no refusal, contradicting the line the diff rewrote six lines above; the wiring IOU assigned to this slice stays open
why: The diff changed line 91 to say Jira tracker_create sends formatted text and refuses an unknown fix version, but the step the spinoff caller actually follows (line 97) was left saying plain text with no `refused: true` handling, and `.claude/wiring-ious.md:13` anchors exactly this fix to 0005's Seams row for the existing modes.
fix: Rewrite step 3 to say the description is sent as formatted text (Markdown) on Jira and that an unknown `fix_version` comes back `refused: true` with nothing created, then tick the IOU line in `.claude/wiring-ious.md` (add that file to Scope or record why not).
evidence: SKILL.md:91 "On Jira, `tracker_create` sends the description as formatted text and refuses an unknown fix version before it creates." vs SKILL.md:97 "a plain-text `description` carrying the pain + why-deferred/what-unblocks"; .claude/wiring-ious.md:13 "- [ ] `adapters/tracker/jira/api.py` `_op_create` fix-version refusal and Markdown description -> anchor: plan \"docs/afk/small-lane/plan/0005-bug-mode.md\" ## Seams ... spinoff step 3 (`skills/afk/to-ticket/SKILL.md`) still calls its `description` plain text and names no `refused: true` answer for an unknown `fix_version`; 0005 owns that file and its existing modes"; adapters/tracker/jira/api.py:695 `refusal, version_warning = _check_fix_versions(project, [p["fix_version"]], "tracker_create")`

finding: Possible hidden coupling: the script uses the github-issues adapter's private `_gh` and `_repo_args` (and Jira's `resolve_creds_env`) via getattr, past the `tracker_api.load` required-names check, and only stubs cover it
why: Every GitHub Issues create runs the type check (the type defaults to bug), so renaming either private helper in the adapter, which no adapter CONTRACT.md declares, would make every GitHub create refuse, and the 40 stub tests would still pass because they fake `_gh`/`_repo_args` themselves.
fix: Pass the names to `tracker_api.load(("call", ...))` per kind, or add a test that loads the real github-issues and jira api modules and checks `_gh`, `_repo_args` and `resolve_creds_env` exist with the expected signatures; better, record these in each adapter's CONTRACT.md as names a publisher may use.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:113 "gh, repo_args = getattr(run.tracker, \"_gh\", None), getattr(run.tracker, \"_repo_args\", None)"; :107 "creds = getattr(run.tracker, \"resolve_creds_env\", lambda: {})() or {}"; :321 "tracker = tracker_api.load((\"call\",))"; scripts/tracker_api.py:10 "`load(required=...)` fails with the missing names ... rather than raising an AttributeError deep inside a publish"; scripts/tests/test_publish_bug_mode.py:146,149 "def _repo_args(self):" / "def _gh(self, *args):" (stub); adapters/tracker/github-issues/CONTRACT.md has no `_gh`/`_repo_args` mention (grep)

finding: Proof files are staged with the work id from before the folder move, so a re-run after a failed proof comment uploads the files again under new names
why: _stage runs before _execute, so the first run uploads `bug-…-p-1-proof-x`; the re-run's work id is now the key, its stored() check looks for `PROJ-1-p-1-proof-x`, finds nothing and calls tracker_attach again.
fix: Stage the proof files after the move, or match stored attachments on a name that does not depend on the work id.
evidence: Probe (Jira create with --proof P-1; attach answers 'the files are attached; the comment failed' and the proof note comment answers 503): first run 'FAILED: step proof: HTTP 503: down', attachments ['bug-export-drops-row-p-1-proof-shot.png']; re-run code 0, attachments ['bug-export-drops-row-p-1-proof-shot.png', 'PROJ-1-p-1-proof-shot.png']. Code: `staged = _stage(plan)` before `_execute(run, plan, resolve, staged)`.

finding: Two description files in the same folder share one marker, so the second run returns the first ticket and files nothing
why: In description mode the work id is the parent folder name, so the create marker `afk-evidence {folder} ticket` is the same for every description in that folder, and the read-first search reports the first ticket as 'found by its marker'.
fix: Derive the description-mode work id from the file too (for example the folder plus the file stem), or refuse a second description in a folder that already has a marked ticket.
evidence: Probe S5 (docs/adhoc/a.md then docs/adhoc/b.md, different text): second run 'PLAN: ticket — create {"summary": "Import ignores the header", ...}', then 'STEP: ticket — PROJ-1 found by its marker, not created again', 'TICKET: PROJ-1 ...', code 0; issues ['PROJ-1']. Code: `work_id = source.resolve().parent.name`.

finding: A re-run with --in-review is refused once the ticket is already in review, even though the in-review step is listed
why: _preflight resolves the in-review target before checking the listed `in-review: <key>` entry, and its fallback compares the ticket's status name to the configured transition value (a transition id or name, not a status name), so a ticket already in review whose workflow has no self-transition is refused.
fix: Skip the preflight target check when `in-review: <key>` is listed, and compare the current status against the matching transition's `to.name`, not against the configured value.
evidence: Probe S4 (config in-review='31'; from 'In Review' the stub offers only 'Back to dev (21)'): first run 'STEP: in-review — moved', 'listed in-review: True'; re-run code=1 'REFUSED: PROJ-9 offers no transition matching the in-review value `31`; it offers: Back to dev (21); nothing was written'. Code: `if in_review and target_key: target = _in_review_target(...)` and `if not _bad(state) and _in_state(state, ("status", value)): return ("status", value)`.

finding: The unique-proof-name loop (design ADR-0004 "unique names") is never entered by any test
why: The only proof tests pass files with different basenames (grid.png, run.log), so the collision branch is dead in the suite; a mutant turning it into `while False:` left all tests green, so two same-kind files with one basename would upload under one name unnoticed.
fix: Add a test passing two proof files of the same kind and basename from different folders (e.g. P-1 a/run.log and P-1 b/run.log) and assert the staged names are `...-p-1-proof-run.log` and `...-p-1-proof-run-2.log`.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:518-523 `base = f"{plan.work_id}-{kind_name.lower()}-proof-{Path(path).name}"` / `while name.lower() in names:` / `name = f"{stem}-{n}.{ext}" if dot else f"{base}-{n}"`; test_publish_bug_mode.py:370 `proof=(("P-3", str(shot)), ("P-1", str(log)))`

finding: The evidence marker is built from the work id, which changes when a deferred folder move finally happens, so a re-run posts the evidence comment again
why: When the first run leaves the folder in place (NOTE: could not be resolved / already exists), evidence is listed as `afk-evidence bug-… evidence`; a later run moves the folder, sets the work id to the key, and neither the listed entry nor the comment read-back matches the new marker.
fix: Keep the markers on the work id the ticket was filed under (for example the key once recorded, or the id from the `ticket:` entry), or check both the old and the new marker before writing.
evidence: Probe S6: first run with resolve returning None, 'NOTE: the spec folder for PROJ-1 could not be resolved', 'STEP: evidence — comment posted'; re-run with resolve, 'STEP: ticket — spec folder moved ...; the work id is now PROJ-1', 'STEP: evidence — comment posted'; 'comments on PROJ-1: 2'. Code: `marker = lambda step: f"afk-evidence {plan.work_id} {step}"` and `_move` sets `plan.work_id = plan.key`.

finding: A diagnosis with no `## Ticket key` or `## Outside writes` heading passes preflight, then fails after the ticket is created, and every re-run fails the same way
why: check_diagnosis treats empty-allowed parts as optional (a missing heading reads as empty), so the absent heading is only found by _write_part (raises Refused after create: exit 1 'nothing was written') or append_outside_write (ValueError after create: exit 2), and a re-run finds the ticket by marker and hits the same error forever.
fix: In _preflight, refuse a diagnosis that lacks the `## Ticket key`, `## Work id` or `## Outside writes` heading before any write.
evidence: Probe S2 (Ticket key heading removed): 'S2 check ok: True', then 'STEP: ticket — PROJ-1 created', 'REFUSED: the diagnosis has no `## Ticket key` part; nothing was written', writes ['tracker_create']. Probe S3 (Outside writes heading removed): first run 'FAILED: the diagnosis has no `## Outside writes` part'; re-run 'STEP: ticket — PROJ-1 found by its marker, not created again' then the same FAILED. Code: `_list(run, plan, f"ticket: {plan.key}")` / `_write_part(plan.source, "Ticket key", plan.key, only_empty=True)` after `_create`.

criterion: Acceptance: The mode creates or updates a bug or ad-hoc ticket ... (PRD AC-031); Evidence goes on the ticket as comments built from the diagnosis and the proof (PRD AC-033); a later different key is listed in Outside writes (SDD §4)
finding: Updating a later, different ticket posts no evidence: the skip check matches the earlier ticket's `evidence:` entry because the marker has no ticket key, and the run still prints TICKET with exit 0
why: The run reports a successful update of the new ticket, but that ticket gets no evidence comment or proof. This breaks AC-031 and AC-033 for the 'later different key' path that the bullet asks the mode to support.
fix: When the target key differs from the recorded key, make the skip check key-specific: either name the step per target ticket (for example `evidence-<key>`, inside the marker's `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*` step grammar) or decide by a marker read-back on the target ticket instead of the listed entry. Add a stub test that checks the new ticket gets the evidence comment.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:532 `marker = lambda step: f"afk-evidence {plan.work_id} {step}"`; :653-656 `entry = f"evidence: {marker}"` / `if not plan.description and listed(plan.source, entry): run.say(f"STEP: {step} — skipped, listed in Outside writes"); return` (same at :664-667 for proof). Reproduced with the test stubs: first run on recorded PROJ-2, then run with key='PROJ-3' -> code 0, lines '... STEP: ticket — PROJ-3 listed in Outside writes', 'STEP: evidence — skipped, listed in Outside writes', 'TICKET: PROJ-3 ...'; stub.issues['PROJ-3']['comments'] == []

finding: The folder-move test proves only the shutil.move fallback; the `git mv` the acceptance names never runs
why: The tests move a folder under pytest's tmp_path, which is not a git repository (`git -C <basetemp> rev-parse` answers `fatal: not a git repository`), so `git mv` always fails and shutil.move does the move; a mutant replacing `mv` with an unknown git verb left the suite green.
fix: Add one test that `git init`s tmp_path, commits the diagnosis folder, runs a create, and asserts `git status --porcelain` shows a rename (R) to docs/PROJ-1/DIAGNOSIS.md rather than a delete plus an untracked file.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:771-774 `moved = subprocess.run(["git", "mv", "--", str(old), str(new)], cwd=str(old.parent), ...) if moved.returncode != 0: shutil.move(str(old), str(new))`; test_publish_bug_mode.py:247-248 `moved = tmp_path / "docs" / "PROJ-1" / "DIAGNOSIS.md"` / `assert moved.is_file() and not path.exists()`; contract Acceptance: "git-moves the folder when the path differs"

finding: The command line that BUG-MODE.md runs is untested beyond one argparse error; a dropped or swapped flag survives the suite
why: BUG-MODE.md steps 2 and 4 invoke the script only through its CLI, yet the one main() test asserts only SystemExit, so a mutant passing `ticket_type=None, key=None` from main() left all 40 tests green (probe run, restored byte-for-byte).
fix: Add main() tests that pass --diagnosis/--description, --key, --type, --fix-version, --proof P-n=PATH, --in-review, --consent, --dry-run against a stub (monkeypatch tracker_api.load) and assert the stub's payloads and the printed TICKET/DRY-RUN line; also assert --diagnosis plus --description together exits non-zero.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:804-808 `result = run_bug_mode(args.diagnosis or args.description, description=bool(args.description), ticket_type=args.ticket_type, key=args.key, ...`; test_publish_bug_mode.py:546-548 `def test_the_command_line_needs_exactly_one_input(capsys): with pytest.raises(SystemExit): mode.main(["--type", "bug"])`

criterion: changed pre-existing sentence true of the code it describes (AGENTS.md section ownership)

Same wording at skills/afk/to-ticket/SKILL.md:17.
fix: Say 'never edits the description of an existing ticket' (the ownership fact) instead of 'only comments on an existing one', in AGENTS.md:180 and SKILL.md:17.

finding: Possible gap: every scripted error answer is returned after the stub has already applied the write, so no test sees a comment, attach, edit or transition that failed without landing
why: Stub.call runs the operation before popping a scripted answer, so scripted failures on non-create writes always leave the effect behind and the read-back finds it; the retry-after-an-empty-read-back path is proven only for tracker_create, where test :469 replaces the method outright.
fix: Let a scripted answer optionally skip the underlying operation (e.g. a `fail_without_effect` queue) and add one evidence-comment case asserting sleeps == [5] and two tracker_comment calls after a 5xx that did not land.
evidence: test_publish_bug_mode.py:61-65 `self.calls.append(...)` / `answer = getattr(self, operation)(payload)` / `queued = self.script.get(operation)` / `return queued.pop(0) if queued else answer`; :287 `stub.script["tracker_comment"] = [{"error": True, "status": 502, "body": "bad gateway"}]`

finding: Every test injects the folder resolver, so the real notes-adapter call in `_resolve_folder` (payload keys, `dir` answer key, failure to None) never runs
why: The folder move after a create depends on `_resolve_folder` reading `dir` from `afk_adapter notes resolve`, but all tests pass `resolve=lambda key: str(tmp_path / "docs" / key)`, so a wrong payload key or answer key would silently leave the folder unmoved with only a NOTE.
fix: Add one test that points AFK_CONFIG at a repo-files config with a spec-dir template and calls `mode._resolve_folder("PROJ-1")` (skip when bash is absent), asserting the rendered directory.
evidence: test_publish_bug_mode.py:210 `resolve=lambda key: str(tmp_path / "docs" / key), **options)`; publish_bug_mode.py:255-262 `afk_adapter notes resolve "$1"', "--", json.dumps({"workId": work_id, "ticket": work_id})] ... return answer.get("dir") if isinstance(answer, dict) else None`

finding: On GitHub Issues a client error is retried twice, and the error is shown as 'HTTP 1'
why: The github-issues adapter puts the gh process exit code in `status` (`"status": done.returncode`, adapters/tracker/github-issues/api.py:108), so _permanent's 400-499 test never matches and _why prints `HTTP 1: ...`, against BUG-MODE.md 'A refusal or a 4xx answer is shown and never retried'.
fix: Treat a github-issues error with a non-HTTP status (gh exit code) as permanent unless its body shows a 5xx or a network failure, and label it as a gh exit code in _why.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:171-173 `status = answer.get("status") ... isinstance(status, int) and 400 <= status < 500`; github-issues/api.py:107-109 `if done.returncode != 0: return {"error": True, "status": done.returncode, ...}`; _why line 163 `f"HTTP {answer['status']}: ..."`.

finding: In-review matching is tested by Jira id and GitHub label only; the by-name match and the already-in-state fallback have no test
why: The acceptance says the in-review key matches a transition "by name or id", but JIRA config uses `"31"` (an id) and no test configures a transition name such as `Start review` or a ticket already in the target status, so a regression in the name branch or the fallback at :455-457 would pass.
fix: Add a Jira case with `transitions: {in-review: "start review"}` (case differs) asserting the move, and one with a ticket already `In Review` and no matching transition asserting no tracker_transition write.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:451 `if value in (str(t.get("id")), t.get("label")) or str(t.get("name", "")).lower() == value.lower():`; :455-457 `state = run.call("tracker_get", ...) if not _bad(state) and _in_state(state, ("status", value)): return ("status", value)`; test_publish_bug_mode.py:198 `"transitions": {"in-review": "31"}`

finding: The Jira mismatch report is untested: the Jira stub always answers an empty `mismatches` list
why: The real Jira tracker_attach returns `mismatches` entries when a stored name or type differs, and the script turns each into a NOTE line, but StubJira hard-codes `"mismatches": []`, so a mutant that drops the mismatch loop survived.
fix: Script a StubJira tracker_attach answer with one `mismatches` entry ({file, reason: "stored differently"}) and assert the `NOTE: stored differently, named in the comment:` line names that file.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:706-707 `for item in answer.get("mismatches") or []: run.say(f"NOTE: stored differently, named in the comment: ...` ; test_publish_bug_mode.py:135-136 `return {"ok": True, "attached": [{"file": f} for f in p["files"]], "mismatches": [], "unsupported_files": []}`; adapters/tracker/jira/api.py:803 `mismatches.append({"file": path, "id": att_id, "reason": "stored differently", ...`
